metadata.story_name: North Slope Borough Search and Rescue

specification.unit_of_analysis: Coastal Utqiagvik region + immediate offshore (10–50 km)

specification_fit.cadence: MARGINAL (12 days < daily ideal; but best available)
specification_fit.variables: YES (ice motion, concentration from SAR signature)

gotchas_avoided: Measures ice MOTION (critical for SAR decisions), not just concentration
Radar penetrates cloud cover (Arctic advantage over optical)
Can distinguish ice edge position (important for coastal prediction)
gotchas_hit: 12-day revisit less frequent than ideal for tactical decisions
caveats: LATENCY ISSUE: 3-day lag too slow for emergency SAR response
12-day revisit misses rapid ice dynamics (24-48 hour changes)
Requires SAR processing expertise; raw backscatter not operationally ready
Must pair with NWP forecast for tactical 6-hour prediction
candidates.validation_note: In Stage 0 'Would Work' BUT with latency caveat. Not suitable as sole data source for operational SAR.
candidates.next_step: Use as strategic context (weekly ice trends), but pair with geostationary for tactical latency

candidates.dataset_name: NOAA GFS Regional Weather Model (0.25° resolution)

specification_fit.variables: PARTIAL (wind, pressure; no direct ice motion or sea level)

gotchas_avoided: Real-time latency (6 hours): suitable for operational decisions
Wind forecast drives ice motion predictions
gotchas_hit: Resolution 25 km coarser than ideal for coastal jets/channels
Does not directly observe ice; depends on model coupling
Forecast skill drops rapidly beyond 3–5 days
caveats: Does NOT directly observe sea ice; requires ocean-atmosphere coupling
Coastal wind jets (critical for Utqiagvik) may be under-resolved at 25 km
Forecast uncertainty grows beyond 3–5 days (SAR decision window)
Must validate against satellite ice motion observations
candidates.validation_note: In Stage 0 'Would Work' for weather context; insufficient alone for ice motion prediction
candidates.next_step: Use as forcing for tactical forecast, paired with geostationary satellite ice observations

gotchas_avoided: High resolution (1 km) shows coastal detail
gotchas_hit: ⚠️ OPERATIONAL TRAP: 1-day latency looks fast until you need 6 hours
Does NOT measure ice motion; only concentration
caveats: LATENCY FAILURE: 2-day latency unacceptable for SAR tactical decisions (need 6 hrs)
Concentration alone insufficient; need motion to predict where ice WILL BE
Cloud cover obscures view; gaps possible between passes
Explicitly in Stage 0 'Wouldn't Work' for operational use
candidates.validation_note: Good for retrospective analysis and climatology, NOT for operational SAR (latency too long)
candidates.next_step: Use only for historical context. For operational decisions, need geostationary or NWP forecast.

recommendation.approach: HYBRID: (1) NOAA GFS regional model for 6-hour forecast skill window (operational). (2) Geostationary satellite imagery (GOES/HIMAWARI) for continuous ice-edge tracking (real-time). (3) Sentinel-1 SAR for strategic weekly ice-motion context. This stacks operational forecast with satellite observation.
recommendation.best_dataset: GFS forecast + geostationary satellite (not in earthdata-mcp; external)
recommendation.operational_requirement: ⚠️ CRITICAL: Polar-orbiting satellites (Sentinel-1, MODIS) have 2–3 day latency. SAR needs 6-hour forecast horizon. earthdata-mcp datasets alone INSUFFICIENT for operational SAR decisions.
refusals: MODIS ice products unsuitable: 2-day latency exceeds 6-hour requirement
Sentinel-1 as sole source: 12-day revisit + 3-day latency misses tactical window
data_gaps: Geostationary satellite ice-edge tracking: NOAA GOES or Japan's HIMAWARI (not in earthdata-mcp)
Real-time ocean inundation model: requires coupled forecast system, not satellite-only
Coastal jet forecast skill: GFS 25 km may miss mesoscale channeling
recommendation.confidence: MEDIUM (0.65). earthdata-mcp datasets provide strategic context but NOT operational SAR response data. Real-time requirement gates performance.

stage_3_exploration_spec.test_region: Utqiagvik coast, Beaufort Sea (bbox: -157.8 to -156.2°W, 71.0 to 71.3°N)
stage_3_exploration_spec.test_method: Tactical forecast test: use GFS wind forecast to predict ice motion; validate with Sentinel-1 SAR observations (weekly)
exploratory_queries: Does GFS 6-hour wind forecast skill translate to ice motion prediction?
What is coastal wind jet bias in 25 km GFS over Beaufort Sea?
Can Sentinel-1 12-day observation validate GFS forecast drift?
What is SAR processing latency in operational pipeline (3 days → ?? hours)?
success_criteria: GFS forecast skill ≥ 80% for wind speed (vs ground truth or reanalysis)
Wind forecast translates to ice position accuracy ±10 km at 6-hour horizon
Sentinel-1 observations consistent with GFS-predicted drift (when available)
Latency pathway identified to meet 6-hour requirement
expected_gotchas: Coastal jets highly sensitive to topography; 25 km model may underresolve
Sea-ice-wind coupling nonlinear; forecast drift can accelerate
Sentinel-1 12-day gap makes validation difficult; need supplementary obs
Latency chain (acquisition → processing → delivery) likely > 6 hours for SAR urgency
